text:
maria: Heads up — since 03:00 UTC we've been seeing repeated p95 latency oscillations on apac-edge GPU rack r17. Spikes line up with a single tenant (tenant-legacy) doing large batching jobs.

sahil: I see the alert, digging into telemetry now. Is this purely GPU-bound or something else (egress, NVLink)?

ops-bot: [ALERT] apac-edge/rack-r17: p95 inference latency > 700ms for 10m (rule: infra.latency.p95)

ryan: NVLink saturation was my first guess. r17 hosts mixed MIG and non-MIG pods; we've seen jitter when large non-interactive batch jobs start stealing PCIe/NVSwitch bandwidth.

chandra: Can someone paste the GPU metrics window (util, mem bw, nvlink bw) for the spike period?

maria: pasted a short snapshot:
```
2026-03-21T03:05:12Z rack=r17 gpu0 util=92 mem_bw=120GB/s nvlink=78Gb/s
2026-03-21T03:05:12Z rack=r17 gpu1 util=30 mem_bw=20GB/s nvlink=12Gb/s
2026-03-21T03:05:12Z rack=r17 gpu2 util=95 mem_bw=130GB/s nvlink=80Gb/s
```

maria: note the bimodal util distribution — looks like two big jobs colliding on separate cards but sharing PCI/NVSwitch.

ryan: that matches noisy-neighbor at the fabric layer. When we colocate big batch replicas + low-latency clients on the same rack, NVSwitch arbitration causes tail spikes.

chandra: immediate mitigation options: 1) soft-evict batch replicas from r17 to a burstable pool, 2) tag tenant-legacy with lower NIC+NVLink qos for now, 3) migrate low-latency pods off that rack. Which do we want for a quick rollback?

maria: prefer (1) and (3) short-term. Can we drain batch replicas with minimal rollbacks?

sahil: I can trigger a targeted placement reschedule for batch jobs to the "ephemeral-burst" pool. Command I'll run:
```
apictl placement reschedule --rack r17 --label job=batch --to-pool ephemeral-burst --grace 120s
```

ryan: +1, do that and watch the p95. Also add a temporary placement rule to prevent new batch pods landing on racks with low-latency traffic: `placement.sensitive=true`.

ops-bot: user sahil invoked placement reschedule (job=batch) on rack r17

maria: running a quick check to see which tenants will be moved: tenant-legacy (4 replicas), analytics-batch (2 replicas).

chandra: While reschedule goes, I'll prepare a follow-up: long-term we should (A) avoid mixed MIG/non-MIG on the same NVSwitch domain, (B) add a fabric-aware scheduler weight, (C) expose nvlink usage per-tenant on the console.

sahil: Reschedule started. Initial progress: 3/6 replicas moved, 2 in progress, 1 respecting pod disruption budget. p95 dropping to ~220ms after first two moves. :thumbsup:

maria: nice. Can we also surface a short postmortem in #incidents once things stabilize? I want action items and owners.

ryan: I'll take the owner for fabric-aware scheduler proposal. Chandra — can you take metrics surface (nvlink per-tenant + alert tweak)?

chandra: Yep, putting a checklist in the doc. Quick note: add a temporary alert to detect NVLink asymmetry per-rack (gpu_util bimodality) so we catch these earlier. Example rule idea: `infra.gpu.util.bimodal > 0.25`

maria: Thanks. Action items: sahil — finish reschedule and confirm p95 stable; ryan — start design doc for scheduler weight; chandra — add nvlink metrics + alert; i'll draft incident summary.

sahil: reschedule complete, p95 for rack r17 steady at 180ms for last 5m. I'll leave the temp placement rule for 1h and then revert.

maria: Great. If this recurs we'll consider carving tenant-legacy into a dedicated slice or adding stricter pool isolation. For now closing loop after the incident doc. :white_check_mark:

ryan: FYI I'll prototype a shim to tagged pods with `fabric.priority` which the scheduler can honor. Not an immediate fix but should help long-term.

chandra: Dropping the bug/epic links in thread: https://intra.redwood/infra/issue/6789 and dashboard: https://telemetry.redwood/apac/rack/r17/nvlink

maria: thanks all — nice quick coordination.
